facts.fact: 酸糖应急袋洒了一地：袋子是她「低血糖或需要把注意力从脑内尖叫的空洞上挪开」时的急救包；捡回的糖沾满灰没法吃，她心疼要补货。
facts.anchor: The baggie catches on something in my purse and slips from my grip, scattering neon-colored sweets across the ugly carpeting.

facts.fact: 税务部 Nadia 跪地帮捡糖、顺势邀她去酒吧——两人入职以来说过约五句话；她鬼使神差答应了：来蒙特利尔几周第一次社交。
facts.anchor: “A bunch of us are heading to the bar,” she continues, undeterred by my silence.

facts.fact: 第一反应是拒绝（企业斯德哥尔摩）；答应的算法是 payday、公寓只有一瓶没开的便宜红酒、以及「不想一个人坐在随机酒吧显得可悲」。
facts.anchor: It’s like some kind of corporate Stockholm Syndrome—trapped together in fluorescent lighting until you convince yourself you actually enjoy each other’s company.

facts.fact: 桌上被连环追问：家庭一问让她「No」出口太利；Chris 再问时真话漏出：「No one. Foster care.」——满桌同情，Tyler 用 IT 话题解围。
facts.anchor: “No.” The word comes out sharper than I intend, and I sip my drink again to cover the awkwardness.

facts.fact: 她灌酒想灌到「不必再扮演人类」；自认 Montréal Mule 尚可。
facts.anchor: Maybe if I get drunk enough, I’ll stop feeling like I’m performing humanity rather than experiencing it.

facts.fact: 第二杯一上，身体造反：胃里沉石、发热出汗、灯光如针——每个细胞都在喊要独处。
facts.anchor: But as my second drink arrives, something shifts in my gut.

facts.fact: 关键顿悟成段：她要的不是回家，是上床做梦——想被那个 presence 看着、想体验「被看见」的舒适；睡眠从逃生变成目的地。
facts.anchor: I want to feel that presence watching me, to experience the comfort of being seen by someone.

facts.fact: 忘了改期的 Voss 第二通电话成了完美逃生借口；电话里继续撒谎「一切都一样」；回家被窥感更强，她「带着饥饿的需求欢迎睡眠」，睡前想白纱后的人——「我想我笑了」。
facts.anchor: “I have to take this,” I say, already standing, relief rushing through me at the perfect excuse.
